mainTopic: How the twenty-אמה limit is measured, and which size אמה is used for סוכה, מבוי, and כלאים
overview: רבא holds that the twenty-אמה limit for a סוכה and a מבוי is measured by the open space (חלל) underneath the סכך or the beam. רב פפא supports this from a ברייתא that uses the entrance of the היכל as its model. רב שימי בר רב אשי objects from a source that says the beam is placed 'from twenty and below.' The answer is that 'below' refers to the lower limit of ten טפחים, which is also measured by the open space. Next, אביי quotes רב נחמן: the אמה of סוכה and מבוי has five טפחים, while the אמה of כלאים has six, so each choice is the strict one. The גמרא tests this with minimum measurements where that אמה would actually be lenient: the length of a מבוי, רבי's four-by-four סוכה, and densely planted vines under רבי שמעון. Each time it answers either that רב נחמן follows the other opinion, or that he meant only 'most of the אמות.' רבא then reports רב נחמן differently: every אמה has six טפחים, but some are measured with spread fingers and some with fingers pressed together. A ברייתא is brought to challenge רבא's version, and it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבא: the measurement is the inner space
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that both the סוכה rule and the מבוי rule in the משנה measure the open space underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: What we learned about a סוכה refers to the space of the סוכה. What we learned about a מבוי refers to the space of the מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating רבא's position. The twenty-אמה limit counts only the empty space underneath, not the top of the roofing or beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a סוכה above twenty אמות is פסול, and a מבוי beam above twenty must be lowered. רבא explains that 'twenty' means the height of the open air below the סכך or קורה. So if the beam's bottom edge is within twenty, it is fine even if its top rises higher.

keyTerms.meaning: the empty, open space (inside or underneath)
we learned in the משנה
an alleyway; it needs a beam or post at its entrance so one may carry in it on שבת
the booth used on סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the rest of this passage tries to prove and then challenge: the measurement is taken at the bottom of the beam or roofing.

phrases.english: We learned about the space of the sukka,
phrases.notes: The twenty-אמה limit for a סוכה measures the open space under the סכך.

phrases.notes: The twenty-cubit limit for the alley beam measures the space beneath the beam.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The twenty-אמה limit for both סוכה and מבוי is measured by the open space beneath the roofing or beam.

steps.title: רב פפא brings support from the Sanctuary entrance
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא cites a ברייתא that compares the מבוי to the entrance of the היכל, whose open space was exactly twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: A ברייתא was taught that supports you. 'An alleyway whose beam is higher than twenty אמות, higher than the entrance of the היכל, must be lowered.' And the entrance of the היכל itself had an open space of twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a ברייתא to prove רבא is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the entrance of the היכל as its model for the twenty-אמה limit. That entrance was twenty אמות of open space, while the lintel above it reached higher than twenty. So the model being copied is 'twenty of open space,' exactly as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
which supports you
the Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
its entrance / doorway
he must reduce (lower) it

steps.confusionAlert: 'Higher than the entrance of the היכל' and 'higher than twenty אמה' mean the same thing here. The ברייתא gives the היכל entrance as the source and model for the number twenty.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,
A baraita was taught that supports you:
An alleyway that is higher than twenty cubits,
phrases.notes: Meaning its cross beam is higher than twenty cubits.

And the Sanctuary itself, its space was twenty.
phrases.notes: The open space of the entrance was twenty, while the lintel above it went higher.

steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the twenty-אמה limit measures the open space.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא modeling the מבוי limit on the entrance of the היכל, whose open space was twenty אמות.

steps.title: רב שימי objects: the beam goes from twenty and below
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר רב אשי cites a source saying the beam is placed from the twenty mark downward, which means the whole beam must be within twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר רב אשי objected to רב פפא: How would he do it? He places the beam from the edge of twenty and below!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי attacks רב פפא's support for רבא with a source that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the beam is placed 'from the edge of twenty and below,' then its top may be at twenty at most, so the entire beam sits within twenty. That means the measurement is taken at the top of the beam, not the open space underneath. This contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from an earlier source)
how?
cross beam over the alley entrance
from the edge of

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Rav Ashi raised an objection to Rav Pappa:

phrases.notes: The whole beam is within twenty, so nothing may stick out above it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב פָּפָּא

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source puts the entire beam below the twenty mark, so its top edge is what is measured, not the space beneath it.

steps.title: רב פפא changes the wording to 'and above'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers by changing the text: the beam is placed from twenty and upward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and above.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself by changing the wording of the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the text reads 'from the edge of twenty and above,' then the bottom of the beam sits at twenty and the beam rises above it. That fits רבא exactly, since the open space underneath is twenty.

keyTerms.meaning: say instead (correcting the text)
and above

phrases.english: Say: 'and above.'
phrases.notes: The beam starts at twenty and goes upward, so the space beneath it is twenty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source says the beam is placed below twenty, so the whole beam must be within twenty.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'and above': the beam's bottom is at twenty, which matches the open-space rule.

steps.title: But the text clearly says 'below'
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי rejects the change of wording because the source explicitly says 'below.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'below'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי pushes back on רב פפא's answer. You cannot just flip the text to say the opposite of what it says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing a word is one thing, but turning 'below' into 'above' reverses the meaning completely. So the emendation seems forced. The next step gives a better answer without changing the text.

keyTerms.meaning: but surely

phrases.english: But 'below' is taught!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The emendation answer only, not רבא's underlying rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The emendation contradicts the explicit wording of the source.

steps.title: Below works like above: the lower limit also measures the open space
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the ברייתא's word 'below' and reads it as the lower limit of ten טפחים. That limit, like the upper limit of twenty, measures the open space under the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא teaches us: the rule below is like the rule above. Just as above, the open space must be no more than twenty, so too below, the open space must be at least ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב שימי's objection without changing the words of the ברייתא. He explains that 'below' refers to the lower height limit of the beam, not to where the beam sits inside the twenty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי thought 'below twenty' meant the whole beam must sit under the twenty mark. רבא reads the ברייתא as setting up a parallel between the two limits: the top limit (twenty אמות) and the bottom limit (ten טפחים). Both measure the open space beneath the beam, so רבא's original rule from Step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us. It introduces the true meaning of a source.
Below. Here it means the lower height limit of the beam.
Above. Here it means the upper height limit of the beam.
Its open space, meaning the empty air under the beam.

steps.whatToRemember: Both height limits of a מבוי beam, at most twenty אמות and at least ten טפחים, are measured by the open space under the beam, not by the beam itself.
steps.confusionAlert: The twenty is measured in אמות and the ten is measured in טפחים. They are different units, so do not mix them up.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

steps.title: Which size cubit is used for סוכה, מבוי, and כלאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רב נחמן: the אמה of סוכה and of מבוי is five טפחים, while the אמה of כלאים is six טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said in the name of רב נחמן: the אמה of סוכה and the אמה of מבוי is an אמה of five טפחים. The אמה of כלאים is an אמה of six טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: how big an אמה is in different areas of הלכה. אביי reports רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For סוכה and מבוי, the twenty-אמה limit is a maximum, so a smaller אמה makes the maximum lower and is stricter. For כלאים, the required distances are minimums, so a larger אמה is stricter. It seems רב נחמן always picks the strict option.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of length.
A small cubit of five טפחים (handbreadths).
A large cubit of six טפחים.
Forbidden mixtures of different kinds of seeds planted together.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the סוגיא, which tests whether the small אמה for מבוי is always the strict choice.

phrases.english: Abaye said in the name of Rav Nachman:
The cubit of a sukkah and the cubit of an alleyway
is a cubit of five handbreadths;
the cubit of diverse kinds
is a cubit of six handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It starts a new topic about the size of the אמה used in the משנה and in other areas of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכה and מבוי use a five-טפחים אמה. כלאים uses a six-טפחים אמה.

steps.title: Which מבוי laws use the small cubit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific מבוי law the five-טפחים אמה applies to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אמה of a מבוי is an אמה of five טפחים. For which law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: the מבוי has several measurements, so which one uses the small אמה? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מבוי has more than one measurement in אמות. The גמרא wants to pin down where רב נחמן's small אמה applies, so it can check whether that choice is always strict.

keyTerms.meaning: For which law? This asks what practical rule a statement is about.

phrases.english: The cubit of an alleyway is a cubit of five handbreadths:
for what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks where exactly the rule from Step 7 about the מבוי applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which measurements of a מבוי are made with the five-טפחים אמה.

steps.title: The small cubit applies to the height and the breach
steps.stepSummary: The small אמה is used for the beam's height (at most twenty אמות) and for a breach in the מבוי wall (at most ten אמות).
steps.simpleTranslation: For its height, and for a breach in the מבוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The small אמה applies to the height of the beam and to a gap in the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these are maximums: the beam may be no higher than twenty אמות, and a breach may be no wider than ten אמות. Measuring with a smaller אמה makes each maximum smaller, so in both cases the small אמה is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Height. Here it means the height of the beam over the מבוי.
A breach, meaning a gap in the wall of the מבוי.

phrases.english: For its height
phrases.notes: The beam may be at most twenty אמות high.

phrases.english: and for the breach of an alleyway.
phrases.notes: A breach may be at most ten אמות wide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question asked in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The height of the beam and the width of a breach, both of which are maximum limits.

steps.title: The minimum length of a מבוי would make the small cubit lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a מבוי must be at least four אמות long, and measuring that minimum with small אמות would be a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the length of a מבוי, which must be four אמות, and there the small אמה is a leniency!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: there is another מבוי measurement, its minimum length of four אמות. For a minimum, a small אמה is lenient, not strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן seemed to always choose the strict measurement. But a minimum of four small אמות is shorter than four large אמות, so a shorter מבוי would qualify, which is lenient. This challenges the idea that the small אמה for מבוי is always the strict choice.

keyTerms.meaning: The length of the מבוי.
Toward leniency, meaning the easier result.
But isn't there...? This introduces a challenge that points to a case that was left out.

steps.confusionAlert: A small אמה is strict for a maximum but lenient for a minimum. The challenge depends on noticing that the length rule is a minimum.

phrases.english: But isn't there the length of an alleyway
of four cubits,
phrases.notes: This is the minimum length for a מבוי.

phrases.english: which would be a leniency!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא מֶשֶׁךְ מָבוֹי בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, דִּלְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the answer in Step 9 and the strict pattern of רב נחמן's ruling in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the small אמה for מבוי is a strict ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The four-אמה length is a minimum. Measuring it with a small אמה lets a shorter מבוי qualify, which is lenient. This goes against רב נחמן's pattern of being strict.

steps.title: רב נחמן holds a מבוי only needs four טפחים in length
steps.stepSummary: The challenge from the minimum length of a מבוי does not apply, because רב נחמן follows the view that this minimum is four טפחים, not four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the one who said a מבוי needs only four טפחים in length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10. According to this answer, רב נחמן follows the opinion that a מבוי's minimum length is measured in טפחים, not אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the minimum length is four אמות, because only then would small אמות make things easier. If the minimum is four טפחים, no אמה is involved at all. So every אמה that does appear in מבוי laws stays strict when it is measured small.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the one who said; following the opinion of
Handbreadths

phrases.english: Like the one who said
phrases.notes: This points to an opinion someone already holds about how long a מבוי must be at minimum.

phrases.english: four handbreadths.
phrases.notes: The minimum length is four טפחים, not four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places רב נחמן within a dispute: he follows the opinion where the problem never comes up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מבוי must be four אמות long, so small אמות would make it easier.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן holds that the minimum is four טפחים, so no lenient use of the small אמה exists.

steps.title: Alternatively, רב נחמן spoke only about most of the measurements
steps.stepSummary: Even if a מבוי must be four אמות long, רב נחמן's rule was meant only for most of the אמות in מבוי laws, not every single one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the minimum is four אמות, and רב נחמן was only talking about most of the אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge. Here it accepts that the minimum length is four אמות, but says רב נחמן's rule was never meant to cover every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, the four-אמה minimum is measured with large six-טפח אמות, which is the strict way. The 'small אמה' rule covers the beam height and the breach, which are most of the cases. It does not cover this exception.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say; introduces a second answer
Most, the majority
He is saying

steps.confusionAlert: This second answer does not reject the four-אמות view. It accepts that view and limits how far רב נחמן's general rule reaches.

steps.title: Which סוכה laws use the five-טפחים אמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to the סוכה half of רב נחמן's statement and asks which law it applies to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אמה of a סוכה is an אמה of five טפחים. For which law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the other half of רב נחמן's statement from step 7, about סוכה. It asks which specific סוכה measurement uses the small אמה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern used for מבוי in step 8. A small אמה only makes sense where it leads to a stricter result, so the גמרא wants to know exactly where that happens in סוכה laws.

steps.title: For the סוכה's height and for a curved wall
steps.stepSummary: The small אמה is used for the maximum height of twenty אמות and for the four-אמה limit of a דופן עקומה. In both cases, a smaller אמה is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: For its height, and for a curved wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the small אמה is used for two סוכה laws: the maximum height and the rule of a curved wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה may not be taller than twenty אמות, so measuring with smaller אמות lowers the limit. Under the דופן עקומה rule, up to four אמות of invalid סכך next to a wall is treated as part of the wall, so smaller אמות allow less invalid סכך. Both results are stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Height
A 'curved wall': invalid סכך next to a wall, treated as if the wall bends inward

phrases.english: For its height,
phrases.notes: The maximum of twenty אמות.

phrases.english: and for a curved wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The maximum height of the סוכה and the four-אמה limit of a דופן עקומה. In both, small אמות are stricter.

steps.title: The minimum size of a סוכה would become more lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a סוכה must be at least four אמות long, and small אמות would make that minimum easier to reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the length of a סוכה, which must be four אמות. That would be a leniency!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 14. If every סוכה אמה is small, then the minimum size of a סוכה would also be measured small, which is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as the one about מבוי in step 10. For a minimum size, a smaller אמה makes the required space smaller, which is the opposite of the strict result we saw for height and the curved wall.

steps.title: רבי's ברייתא: a סוכה must be at least four אמות by four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא in which רבי rules that a סוכה smaller than four by four אמות is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, I say that any סוכה that does not have four אמות by four אמות is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the fact behind its challenge: a סוכה really does need a minimum area of four by four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source shows that there is a real minimum size for a סוכה measured in אמות. That gives the challenge in step 15 something solid to stand on: here is an actual law where the small אמה would be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
רבי יהודה הנשיא
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: For both מבוי and סוכה, the small אמה works well for upper limits (it makes them stricter). Minimum sizes are the trouble spot, because a small אמה would make them easier.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.english: I say, any sukka
phrases.notes: רבי states his own view.

phrases.notes: The minimum size.

phrases.english: by four cubits is invalid!
phrases.notes: Below this size, the סוכה is invalid.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (continuation of the challenge in step 15)
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי, כׇּל סוּכָּה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת פְּסוּלָה

steps.raayaObject: That a סוכה has a minimum size measured in אמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי: a סוכה smaller than four by four אמות is invalid.

steps.title: רב נחמן follows the רבנן, who require no four-אמה minimum
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds like the רבנן: a סוכה is valid even if it only holds a person's head, most of his body, and his table. So there is no four-אמה minimum that a small אמה would make easier.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the רבנן, who say: a סוכה is valid even if it only holds his head, most of his body, and his table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 15-16 by saying רב נחמן follows the רבנן, not רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if a סוכה must be at least four אמות long, because there a small אמה would be a leniency. According to the רבנן, the minimum size is just enough room for head, most of the body, and a table, which is a measure in טפחים, not in אמות. So every אמה-based rule of סוכה is a maximum, and a small אמה is always stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the majority opinion against רבי)
Holds / has room for
His head and most of his body
His table

phrases.english: He holds like the Rabbis, who say:
even if it does not hold
phrases.notes: "It" = the סוכה.

phrases.english: anything but his head, most of his body, and his table.
phrases.notes: This is commonly understood as seven by seven טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15, which was backed by רבי's ברייתא in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the statement to a different תנא (the רבנן instead of רבי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A סוכה needs a four-אמה minimum, so a small אמה would be a leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the רבנן there is no four-אמה minimum, so the small אמה is always stricter.

steps.title: Even according to רבי, רב נחמן meant most of the סוכה's אמות
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב נחמן can even follow רבי. He only meant that most סוכה measurements use the small אמה. The four-אמה minimum is measured with the large אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: really, it follows רבי, and רב נחמן was speaking about most of the אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer: רב נחמן's rule fits רבי too, because it was never meant for every single אמה of סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא keeps רבי's four-אמה minimum. It says that minimum is measured with large six-טפח אמות, which is the strict choice. The small-אמה rule covers only the other measurements: the twenty-אמה height and the דופן עקומה. This uses the same "most of the אמות" idea the גמרא already used for מבוי in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
Actually / really (keeps the original assumption)
Most of the אמות

steps.whatToRemember: For סוכה the rule is always "go strict." A small אמה is used for maximums. If רבי's four-אמה minimum applies, it is measured with the large אמה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, it follows Rabbi,
and he was speaking about most of the amos.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement (most cases, not all).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant that every אמה of סוכה is the small one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only most of the סוכה measurements use the small אמה. The four-אמה minimum uses the large one.

steps.title: Where is the six-טפח אמה of כלאים used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third part of רב נחמן's statement: the אמה of כלאים is six טפחים. It asks which law this applies to.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The אמה of כלאים is an אמה of six טפחים." For which law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking where in the laws of כלאים the large אמה is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the question about סוכה in step 13. The גמרא wants a case where using the large six-טפח אמה makes the law stricter. That would explain why רב נחמן chose it for כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures, here of seeds planted near a vineyard
An אמה of six טפחים (the large אמה)
For which law?

phrases.english: The amah of kilayim is an amah of six handbreadths,
phrases.notes: This quotes רב נחמן's statement.

phrases.english: for which law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves סוכה behind and opens the כלאים section of רב נחמן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which כלאים law uses the six-טפח אמה.

steps.title: For the vineyard clearing and the vineyard border
steps.stepSummary: The large אמה is used for קרחת הכרם, an empty clearing inside a vineyard, and for מחול הכרם, the empty border between a vineyard and its fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is used for the clearing in a vineyard and for the border around a vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the six-טפח אמה is used to measure two empty areas connected to a vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other seeds may be planted in these empty areas only if each area is big enough to count as separate from the vineyard. Measuring with a larger אמה means the area must be physically bigger before planting is allowed. That is why the large אמה is the stricter choice here.

keyTerms.meaning: A bare clearing in the middle of a vineyard
The empty strip between a vineyard and its surrounding fence

steps.confusionAlert: Here the big אמה is the strict one, the opposite of סוכה. Both fit the same rule: always pick the אמה that makes the law stricter.

phrases.english: For the clearing in a vineyard and for the border of a vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six-טפח אמה is used for קרחת הכרם and מחול הכרם.

steps.title: The משנה giving the sizes of the clearing and the border
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in כלאים gives the required sizes. For a clearing: בית שמאי say 24 אמות, בית הלל say 16. For a border: בית שמאי say 16, בית הלל say 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: for a vineyard clearing, בית שמאי say 24 אמות and בית הלל say 16 אמות. For a vineyard border, בית שמאי say 16 אמות and בית הלל say 12 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that shows these two areas are measured in אמות. This is where רב נחמן's large אמה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only when the clearing or border reaches these sizes may one plant other seeds there, keeping a distance from the vines. Because the measurements are minimums needed for permission to plant, a bigger אמה makes them harder to reach. That is stricter, and it fits רב נחמן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל

steps.whatToRemember: In כלאים the large six-טפח אמה is used, because these vineyard areas are minimum sizes. A bigger אמה is stricter there.

phrases.english: As we learned: a clearing in a vineyard,

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: twenty-four amos,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: sixteen amos.
And the border of a vineyard,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: sixteen amos,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: twelve amos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 20 by citing the משנה where these measurements appear.
steps.raayaObject: That קרחת הכרם and מחול הכרם are measured in אמות, as minimum sizes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת כלאים (the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל).

steps.title: The משנה defines a vineyard clearing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what a קרחת הכרם is. If the clearing is less than 16 אמות wide, nothing may be sown there. If it is 16 or more, the vineyard gets its working space and the rest may be sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a clearing in a vineyard? It is a vineyard whose middle was destroyed. If there are not sixteen אמות there, one may not bring seed there. If there are sixteen אמות there, he leaves the vineyard its working space and sows what is left over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה from step 21. Here the משנה explains exactly what a 'clearing' is and when you may plant other crops in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minimum width of 16 אמות is required before any sowing is allowed. Measuring with the larger six-טפח אמה makes the required space bigger, so it is harder to sow. That is a חומרא, which fits רב נחמן's claim that כלאים uses the large אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: became destroyed or bare (the vines died or were removed)
its middle section
seed (another crop that would create כלאים with the vines)
its working space: the strip left empty so the vines can be tended
the leftover area

steps.confusionAlert: Why is the large אמה a חומרא here? The rule says you may sow only if there are 16 אמות. If each אמה is bigger, you need more actual ground before sowing is allowed. So a bigger אמה means fewer clearings qualify, which is stricter.

phrases.english: What is a clearing of the vineyard?
A vineyard whose middle became bare,
if there are not sixteen cubits there,
he may not bring seed there.
phrases.notes: Sowing there would be forbidden כלאים הכרם.

phrases.english: If there were sixteen cubits there,
he gives it (the vineyard) its working space,
phrases.notes: Four אמות next to the vines are left unsown.

phrases.english: and sows the remainder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quoted in step 21 and defines the clearing case.
steps.raayaObject: That קרחת הכרם is measured with the large six-טפח אמה, as a חומרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלאים defining קרחת הכרם

steps.title: The משנה defines a vineyard border
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that מחול הכרם is the space between the vineyard and its fence. Less than 12 אמות means no sowing. With 12 or more, the vineyard gets its working space and the rest may be sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the border of a vineyard? It is the space between the vineyard and the fence. If there are not twelve אמות there, one may not bring seed there. If there are twelve אמות there, he leaves the vineyard its working space and sows the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case: the empty strip between the vines and the surrounding fence, and how wide it must be before you may plant there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure matches the clearing case, but the minimum is 12 אמות instead of 16. Again, a larger אמה means more real ground is needed before sowing is allowed. This is the second example of the large אמה working as a חומרא.

keyTerms.meaning: fence or wall around the vineyard
the rest (same meaning as הַמּוֹתָר)

steps.whatToRemember: Both the clearing (16 אמות) and the border (12 אמות) are minimums before sowing is allowed. With these, a bigger אמה is stricter. This is why רב נחמן's large אמה fits כלאים.

phrases.english: And what is the border of the vineyard?
The space between the vineyard and the fence.
If there are not twelve cubits there,
he may not bring seed there.
If there were twelve cubits there,
he gives it its working space,
and sows the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel definition of the second case in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That מחול הכרם is measured with the large six-טפח אמה, as a חומרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלאים defining מחול הכרם

steps.title: Challenge from vines planted less than four cubits apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב נחמן. In the case of vines planted closely, fewer than four אמות apart, using the large אמה would lead to a leniency. According to רבי שמעון, such a planting is not a vineyard at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of vines planted close together within four אמות, where the large אמה leads to a leniency! As we learned in a משנה: A vineyard planted with less than four אמות between its rows: רבי שמעון says it is not a vineyard. The חכמים say it is a vineyard, and we view the middle rows as if they are not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's rule that all כלאים measurements use the large אמה. It brings a case where a large אמה would make the law more lenient, not stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, rows less than four אמות apart do not count as a vineyard, so sowing nearby is not כלאים הכרם. If each אמה is bigger, more plantings fall under 'less than four,' so more of them lose vineyard status. That is a קולא, and our rule is that a large אמה should only be used where it makes things stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: planted densely, packed close together
resulting in a leniency
as we learned in a משנה
the middle rows (extra rows squeezed in between properly spaced ones)

steps.confusionAlert: Here a bigger אמה is lenient, the opposite of steps 22–23. Under רבי שמעון the rule is 'less than four אמות means not a vineyard.' A bigger אמה makes more plantings count as 'less than four,' so fewer count as a vineyard.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אִיכָּא רְצוּפִים בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, דִּלְקוּלָּא!
phrases.english: But there is the case of densely planted vines within four cubits, which would be a leniency!

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: כֶּרֶם הַנָּטוּעַ עַל פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: As we learned: A vineyard planted with less than four cubits between rows,
Rabbi Shimon says: it is not a vineyard.
And the Sages say: it is a vineyard,
and we view the middle rows as if they are not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא רְצוּפִים בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת דִּלְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from steps 19–23 that the large אמה in כלאים always works as a חומרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that the אמה of כלאים is six טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי שמעון, measuring the 'less than four אמות' rule with the large אמה strips more plantings of vineyard status, which is a קולא.

steps.title: Answer: רב נחמן follows the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds like the חכמים, who say a densely planted vineyard is still a vineyard. So the four-אמה measurement never produces a leniency for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the רבנן, who say it is a vineyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רב נחמן follows the חכמים, not רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, close planting does not cancel vineyard status. Sowing there is forbidden no matter how the four אמות are measured, so the large אמה cannot create a leniency. The challenge only worked under רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: like the רבנן (the חכמים)
it is, it counts as

phrases.english: Like the Rabbis, who say it is a vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by choosing the opinion of the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the statement to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's rule would create a leniency under רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן follows the חכמים, for whom dense planting stays a vineyard, so no leniency arises.

steps.title: Second answer: רב נחמן meant most cubits
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, רב נחמן can follow רבי שמעון. He only meant that most כלאים measurements use the large אמה. The dense-planting case uses the small אמה as a חומרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: Really, he follows רבי שמעון, and he was speaking about most אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer that lets רב נחמן agree even with רבי שמעון. His rule was a general one, not a rule for every single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, the dense-planting case is measured with the small five-טפח אמה so that it stays strict. רב נחמן's 'six טפחים' describes most כלאים measurements, not all of them. This matches the second answer given in step 18 for סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
really, in truth
most of the cubit measurements

steps.whatToRemember: The guiding idea of רב נחמן's rule is that the measurement is chosen to be stricter. Here, either he follows the חכמים, or his 'large אמה' rule covers only most כלאים measurements, and the dense-planting case uses the small אמה to stay strict.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'רוֹב אַמּוֹת' answer shows a pattern in this סוגיא. A general rule about which אמה to use may have exceptions when that אמה would lead to a leniency.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it follows Rabbi Shimon,
and he was speaking about most cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 24, parallel to the answer in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant that every כלאים measurement uses the large אמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant most כלאים measurements. The dense-planting case under רבי שמעון uses the small אמה as a חומרא.

steps.title: רבא's version: every אמה has six handbreadths, measured loose or tight
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: every אמה of the חכמים has six טפחים. The difference is only in how each טפח is measured. In some cases the fingers are spread apart, and in others they are pressed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: all the אמות are an אמה of six handbreadths. Only, these are 'laughing' (spread, generous) and those are 'sad' (squeezed, tight).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב נחמן's view, from רבא instead of אביי. In this report, every אמה has six טפחים, but the way the טפחים are measured changes from case to case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's version, the two kinds of אמה differ in how many טפחים they have: six or five. In רבא's version, they always have six. The only difference is spread fingers (שׂוֹחֲקוֹת, a bit bigger) versus fingers pressed together (עֲצֵבוֹת, a bit smaller). Following the Sefaria explanation, the כלאים measurements use the spread טפחים, and the מבוי and סוכה measurements use the pressed ones.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמה made of six handbreadths
A handbreadth, the width of four fingers
'Laughing': handbreadths measured with the fingers spread apart, so slightly larger
'Sad': handbreadths measured with the fingers pressed together, so slightly smaller

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is arguing with רב נחמן. רבא and אביי disagree about what רב נחמן actually said. Both are reporting the same teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how the two kinds of measurement differ. They no longer differ by a whole טפח, only by a tiny amount from how the fingers are held.

phrases.notes: Measured with fingers spread apart, so a bit bigger. This is the one used for כלאים.

phrases.english: and those are 'sad' (pressed together).
phrases.notes: Measured with fingers squeezed together, so a bit smaller. This is the one used for מבוי and סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב נחמן's statement from אביי's version in step 7, which steps 8-26 analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every אמה has six טפחים. In some cases the טפחים are measured spread out, and in others pressed together.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to challenge רבא's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא: 'All the אמות the חכמים mentioned are six-טפח אמות, provided that...' The text breaks off here, and the challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: All the אמות that the חכמים mentioned are an אמה of six handbreadths, provided that...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by starting to quote a ברייתא. The key condition after 'provided that' comes on the next amud, so the actual attack is not yet visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening of the ברייתא seems to agree with רבא: every אמה is six טפחים. The word וּבִלְבַד ('provided that') tells us a condition is coming. That condition is what will clash with רבא's version of רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged': a formula that brings a תנאי source to object to an אמורא
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
'Provided that': introduces a condition

phrases.english: They challenged:
phrases.notes: This signals a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: All cubits that the Sages mentioned
phrases.notes: The ברייתא speaks about every measurement in general.

phrases.english: are a cubit of six handbreadths, provided that...
phrases.notes: The condition continues on the next amud.
